# Intake Brief — Wave Laser at half its current speed (AH-0MVEXPKU9000SB20)

**Headline:** The Wave Laser's beam should travel at half its current speed —
350 px/s → 175 px/s — declared once in the shared weapon catalogue and resolved
once in the shared combat core, so the game and every gym fire an identical
slower beam. Reach falls with it (~350 → ~175 px) because the beam's lifetime
is unchanged, which the producer confirmed is intended.

- **Type:** `task` (balance tuning — matches the precedent of
  `Reduce bullet speed of enemies` (AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ))
- **Priority:** medium (non-blocking balance tweak; operator did not specify)
- **Scope confirmed:** Q1 = **A** (projectile travel speed, not fire cadence),
  Q2 = **A** (reach halves too; `bulletLifetime` stays 1.0 s) — see Appendix.

## Problem statement

The Wave Laser (`wave_laser`) fires its beam projectile at the shared player
bullet speed of 350 px/s — the same speed as the cannon — so the beam reads as
a fast bolt rather than a slow, heavy laser. The producer wants the beam to
move at **half** its current speed (**175 px/s**), with fire cadence, damage
budget and visuals unchanged.

## Users

- **Player** — gets a visibly slower, heavier beam that can be tracked across
  the playfield instead of snapping to its target.
- **Designer / AI agent** — needs exactly one per-weapon speed seam in the
  catalogue, consumed by the shared combat core, so the game and every gym
  cannot drift apart on this value.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want the wave laser beam to crawl across the playfield at
  half its current speed so that the beam feels like a committed, heavy laser
  rather than a fast cannon bullet.
- As a **developer**, I want the wave laser's speed declared once in
  `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` and resolved once in the shared auto-fire path, so the
  shipped game and `GymWeapons` fire identical beams.

## Existing state (verified in this checkout)

| Fact | Location |
|------|----------|
| All player bullets travel at 350 px/s | `src/core/constants.ts` — `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED = 350`; `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `BULLET_SPEED = 350` |
| The single shared spawn path picks the speed | `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` (~L934): `const speed = def.aoe?.projectileSpeed ?? PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED;` |
| The only per-weapon speed today | `AoEDescriptor.projectileSpeed` (AOE weapons only — Nova/Mortar/Arc) |
| `wave_laser` definition | `src/utils/weapons.ts` — offsets `[0]`, 1 shot/beat (750 ms), `bulletLifetime` 1.0 s, `maxHitPoints` 2, `bulletShape: 'line'` |
| Current effective reach | `BULLET_SPEED 350 × 1.0 s` ≈ 350 px ("crosses the arena") |
| Unused upgrade seam | `bulletSpeed` is already a `WeaponUpgradeVariable` (`src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`, planned tier, base 1, cap 1.8×) but no catalogue field consumes it yet |
| Gym parity | Every gym inherits `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`; `GymWeapons` runs the same auto-fire path (asserted in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) |

## Desired change

Add an optional per-weapon `bulletSpeed` (px/s) to `WeaponDefinition`, resolve
it in the one shared auto-fire spawn path (falling back to
`PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED`), and set `WEAPON_CATALOGUE.wave_laser.bulletSpeed` to an
exported constant of **175** (half of 350). Every other weapon keeps 350 px/s;
the beam's reach consequently falls to ~175 px, which is intended.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Wave laser speed halved in the catalogue.**
  `WeaponDefinition` in `src/utils/weapons.ts` gains an optional `bulletSpeed`
  (px/s, documented as "falls back to `BULLET_SPEED` when absent"); an exported
  `WEAPON_WAVE_LASER_BULLET_SPEED` constant is **175**; and
  `WEAPON_CATALOGUE.wave_laser.bulletSpeed` uses it, so the value is exactly
  `BULLET_SPEED / 2`. Verified by unit tests in `src/utils/weapons.test.ts`
  asserting the constant (175), the halving relationship to `BULLET_SPEED`, and
  that the beam still keeps `bulletLifetime` 1.0 s, `maxHitPoints` 2 and its
  1-shot-per-beat cadence.
- [ ] **AC2 — One shared resolution point for game and gyms.** The shared
  auto-fire spawn path in `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` derives the
  projectile speed as `def.aoe?.projectileSpeed ?? def.bulletSpeed ??
  PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED`, so the shipped game and every gym (including
  `GymWeapons`) fire the same slower beam with no per-scene copy; the pure
  helpers `bulletForShot` / `allBulletsForShot` honour `bulletSpeed` too
  (or are documented as legacy). Verified by asserting the bullet velocity
  magnitude for a wave-laser shot in the game scene (`CombatScene.test.ts`)
  and in the game↔gym parity test (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`), plus
  `GymWeapons.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC3 — No collateral change.** Every other weapon still fires at
  `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` (350 px/s); the wave laser keeps its fire cadence,
  `maxHitPoints` budget (2), `bulletLifetime` (1.0 s), visual metadata
  (`line` shape, thickness, trail, muzzle/impact FX) and level curves. The
  effective-reach change (≈350 → ≈175 px, because speed halved and lifetime is
  unchanged) is documented as intended, not as a defect. Verified by unit
  tests including a catalogue sweep proving only `wave_laser` declares
  `bulletSpeed`, and by the existing tests that pinned "every bullet travels at
  `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED`" now excluding the wave laser.
- [ ] **AC4 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
  site entries — specifically the `wave_laser` entry and the
  `WEAPON_BULLET_LIFETIME`/reach comments in `src/utils/weapons.ts`, the weapon
  catalogue description in `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4, and the R-Type
  wave-laser entry in `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` (speed
  350 → 175 px/s, reach ≈175 px). Any docs-guard test that pins these facts
  (`src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`,
  `src/utils/weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts`,
  `src/powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts`) is updated.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes, including
  the game/gym parity and docs-guard tests.

## Constraints

- **Projectile speed only.** Fire interval (1/beat), damage budget, bullet
  lifetime, visuals, level curves and every other weapon are untouched.
- **Shared core only.** No gym-specific copies; the change must be visible in
  the game and in `GymWeapons` through `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene`.
- **Reach halving is accepted** (producer-confirmed, Q2 = A): `bulletLifetime`
  stays 1.0 s, so the beam reaches ~175 px instead of ~350 px.
- **Enemy projectile tuning is out of scope** (already halved by
  AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ).
- **CHANGELOG.md is excluded** — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.
- Balance is expressed as a constant/definition change, not a new mechanic.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — perceived weapon nerf:** the wave laser is described in the GDD as
  a *long-range* beam, and its reach now halves; the producer explicitly chose
  this (Q2 = A), so the docs must state the new reach plainly rather than
  leaving "crosses the arena" claims in place.
- **Risk — legacy helper drift:** `bulletForShot` / `allBulletsForShot`
  hard-code `BULLET_SPEED` and are used only by tests; honour `bulletSpeed`
  (or document them as legacy) so they don't contradict the live path.
- **Scope-creep risk:** wiring the *planned* `bulletSpeed` level variable
  (`levelBulletSpeed`, cap 1.8×) is **not** required here — record as a
  separate item if wanted rather than expanding this change.
- **Assumption — parity is automatic:** because the speed is resolved in
  `CombatCoreScene`, no gym-specific work is needed beyond parity tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — add optional `bulletSpeed` to `WeaponDefinition`
  (update the `bulletLifetime`/reach comment), export
  `WEAPON_WAVE_LASER_BULLET_SPEED = 175`, set it on the `wave_laser` entry;
  honour it in `bulletForShot`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — resolve
  `def.aoe?.projectileSpeed ?? def.bulletSpeed ?? PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` in the
  shared auto-fire spawn loop (single source of truth for game + gyms).
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` — catalogue value, halving relationship, and a
  sweep asserting no other weapon declares `bulletSpeed`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` — the "every bullet travels at
  `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED`" expectation (L~401) gains a wave-laser carve-out, plus
  a wave-laser velocity assertion.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — game↔gym parity assertion
  for the slower beam (the shared-speed assertion at L~349 gains the same
  carve-out).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — wave-laser beam velocity matches the
  game's.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`,
  and the docs-guard tests listed in AC4.

## Related work

- **Reduce bullet speed of enemies (AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ)** — direct precedent:
  a 50 % projectile-speed cut with lifetimes unchanged and the resulting
  reach halving documented as accepted.
- **Reduce the starting range of all weapons by 50% (AH-0MUU131PU006O7ZD)** —
  the earlier reach-halving pass (lifetime/AOE radii), which set the current
  ~350 px wave-laser reach.
- **R-Type piercing wave laser (AH-0MV1BIUSJ0090W92)** and its bounded
  damage-budget revision (AH-0MV97RISJ002WR2S) — the weapon this tunes.
- **Wave Laser projectile visuals & feel (AH-0MV822ACO007CEZF)** — the visual
  metadata this change leaves untouched.
- **Weapon leveling (parent AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J)** — owns the `bulletSpeed`
  upgrade variable this change deliberately does not wire up.
- **R-Type entry, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`** — documents the
  "long-range, slow cadence, committed shot" identity this change touches.
- Related docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (weapon catalogue),
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (gym↔game parity rule).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which "speed" should be halved?**
  - A. **Projectile travel speed:** beam velocity 350 → **175 px/s**, cadence
    unchanged at 1 shot/beat.
  - B. Fire cadence: keep 350 px/s, fire every 2 beats (1500 ms).
  - C. Both A and B.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-25): "1. A"** — projectile
    travel speed only. Evidence/basis: `src/utils/weapons.ts`
    (`BULLET_SPEED = 350`, wave-laser fire rate 1/beat);
    `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` (~L934) applies `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED`
    to every non-AOE weapon today; precedent AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ used "speed"
    to mean projectile velocity. Recorded in worklog comment
    `AH-C0MVNY20VP006OA7Z`.
- **Q2 — Should the beam keep its reach?**
  - A. **Reach halves too** (≈350 → ≈175 px): change the speed only, leave
    `bulletLifetime` at 1.0 s.
  - B. Preserve reach (≈350 px) by doubling `bulletLifetime` 1.0 → 2.0 s.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-25): "2. A"** — reach halves
    too; lifetime unchanged. Evidence/basis: effective reach is
    `bulletSpeed × bulletLifetime` (`WEAPON_BULLET_LIFETIME.wave_laser = 1.0`);
    GDD §4.4 describes the wave laser as long-range (~350 px) and
    AH-0MUU131PU006O7ZD set the current reach. Recorded in worklog comment
    `AH-C0MVNY20VP006OA7Z`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV1BIUSJ0090W92** – R-Type piercing wave laser (completed)
- **AH-0MV822ACO007CEZF** – Wave Laser projectile visuals & feel (completed)
- **AH-0MV97RISJ002WR2S** – Wave Laser should have limited hit power (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mupmpcb2009j54j, 0muu131pu006o7zd, 0muwz5gst003nmfq, 0mv1biusj0090w92, 0mv97risj002wr2s (+305 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mupmpcb2009j54j, 0mv1biusj0090w92, absent, ac1, ac2 (+292 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0muwz5gst003nmfq, absent, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+272 more)

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-10-28)

**Planning decision:** auto-complete — effort **Small**, risk **Low** (below the
planning threshold), so the item is delivered as a **single end-to-end slice**
(test → catalogue change → shared-core resolution → docs) rather than being
decomposed into child items. Verification lives inside the ACs (AC1/AC2/AC3
unit + parity tests, AC5 full suite), so no separate test-first child is needed.

- **Single vertical slice:** `src/utils/weapons.ts` (`bulletSpeed` field +
  `WEAPON_WAVE_LASER_BULLET_SPEED = 175`) → `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
  (`def.aoe?.projectileSpeed ?? def.bulletSpeed ?? PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED`) →
  tests (`weapons.test.ts`, `CombatScene.test.ts`,
  `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `GymWeapons.test.ts`) → docs (GDD §4.4,
  `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`, docs-guard tests).
- **No dependencies / no children:** nothing blocks this item; it blocks nothing.
- **Open questions:** none — producer answered Q1 = A (projectile travel speed)
  and Q2 = A (reach halves too) in the Appendix above.

# Implement: seam-aware aimed fire

Implementation slice for seam-aware aimed fire (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC2). Every archetype routed through the shared aimed-shot method — Scout, `march` and the Raider — gains shortest-wrapped-path aiming in one place.

## Goal

Compute the player delta along the shortest wrapped path before `atan2` in the shared aimed-fire seam, gated on `wrapAware`, so shots can leave one edge and arrive from the opposite edge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The wrapped-delta calculation lives once in a shared pure helper in `src/scenes/core/` (or alongside `enemyTargeting.ts`) and is imported by the aimed-fire seam — no divergent copy in any entity.
- `Scout.tryFireAimedBullet` aims along the shortest wrapped path when `wrapAware` is true, preserving every existing gate (fire interval, shot probability, advance cue/tell, `shootEnabled`, alive, spawn guard).
- Aimed-fire archetypes sharing the method (`march`, `raider`) inherit the behaviour through the same seam with no per-class copy.
- An enemy with `wrapAware: false` keeps the current direct aim — bit-identical angles for mid-arena geometry.
- Radial/spread/burst patterns are untouched (out of scope per parent constraint).
- The bullet wrap model itself is untouched; only launch direction changes.
- Build passes and the changed-scope tests (including the slice-3 tests) are green.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Scout.ts`
- `src/entities/Raider.ts`
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`

Test-first verification slice for wrap-aware movement (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC3 + AC5). Pins per-edge wrapping for wrap-aware archetypes and the unchanged bounded behaviour of the classic exclusions.

## Goal

Specify, in tests, that wrap-aware motion which would carry an enemy off-screen wraps to the opposite edge while `march` and `centipede` keep their bounded, wall-respecting behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests assert that crossing each of the four edges (left, right, top, bottom) relocates a wrap-aware enemy to the opposite edge, matching the player/asteroid four-edge wrap model (position only — velocity preserved).

# Implement: shared post-motion edge wrap

Implementation slice for wrap-aware movement (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC3). One shared post-motion step wraps wrap-aware enemies across the seam instead of clamping them to the arena.

## Goal

Wrap each wrap-aware enemy's position in the shared scene entity loop (game + gyms), gated on `wrapAware`, so the whole wrapped playfield is the arena for every archetype except the classic exclusions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single shared post-motion wrap step lives in `src/scenes/core/` and is called from the shared entity loop used by both `PlayScene` and the gym scenes — no per-scene or per-entity copy.
- Wrap-aware enemies (dive, chase, orbit, drift, roam, hold-and-move) wrap across the opposite edge when their motion would carry them off-screen; velocity and heading are preserved (no reflection).
- `march` and `centipede` remain unchanged: march reverses and drops at the arena edge, centipede weaves within bounds.
- Formation bases and formation-shaping logic are unchanged — wrapping is entity-level only (per parent risk note).
- Steering that seeks the player remains stable near the seam (no oscillation); the shared wrap does not fight a steering state machine.
- No archetype other than the documented exclusions keeps bounded/clamped motion; any extra exclusion discovered is recorded as a code comment plus a documented divergence.
- Build passes and the changed-scope tests (including the slice-5 tests) are green.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`

## Goal (tracer-bullet vertical slice)

Ship the first end-to-end music slice: the menu/attract ambient track ("Star Drift", Lydian) played through the existing shared AudioContext, driven by a minimal music state machine, with the autoplay/gesture guard and an independent music volume control.

This slice cuts through every layer — baked asset, playback facade, state machine, scene wiring, settings, tests, docs — so later slices extend a proven path rather than a horizontal layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The menu/attract state plays the baked "Star Drift" Lydian ambient stem as a seamless loop.
- [ ] Music starts only after a user gesture, honouring the AudioContext resume discipline (GDD 7.3), and reuses the single shared AudioContext owned by the playback provider.
- [ ] Music volume and mute are independent of SFX and persisted in the settings record.
- [ ] The state machine enters and leaves the menu/attract state only at a bar boundary of the shared beat clock.
- [ ] Unit tests cover stem looping, the gesture guard, independent volume routing and the menu/attract transition; all playback degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext.

- [ ] Covers parent AC5: **Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.

## Minimal implementation

1. Bake the "Star Drift" ambient stem via the ToneForge pipeline and add it to the cue/stem manifest (smallest slice of the stem pipeline).
2. Add src/audio/music/musicPlayer.ts (facade) and a minimal src/audio/music/musicStateMachine.ts with the menu/attract state.
3. Wire gesture-driven start/resume through MenuScene using the shared AudioContext.
4. Extend SettingsRecord with musicVolume/musicMuted and route them independently of SFX.
5. Add unit tests for each acceptance criterion.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by Music contract mapping and traceability guard (AH-0MVMH2OPY001X6M3), which is itself blocked by the chapter docs item (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W).
- Reuses the shared AudioContext and provider seam in src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts.

## Risky assumption

Baked stems (not runtime synthesis) are the delivery mechanism, consistent with the shipped ToneForge pipeline; recorded as an assumption in the parent item's plan.

## Goal (vertical slice)

Extend the proven music path with the Phrygian Dominant combat layer — Combat Motifs A and B and the combat progression — that transitions in from the ambient state at a bar boundary, stays locked to the shared beat grid, ducks under key SFX, and is driven by PlayScene and the gym scenes identically (gym-game parity).

## Acceptance Criteria

# Shard Swarm — fire/impact VFX & SFX

**discovered-from:AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW** (5 net-new weapon types) — audit of the `shard_swarm` player weapon found it shipped with an in-flight bullet look only: no fire sound, no muzzle flash and no per-weapon impact feedback.

## Current state (audit evidence)

Present:
- In-flight identity: `bulletShape: 'shard'` + overrides (`bulletShapeLength: 1.6`, `bulletTrail: 1.2`, `bulletSize: 0.72`, lime `BULLET_COLORS.shard_swarm = 0xc0ff33`) in `src/utils/weapons.ts:1336`, rendered through the shared bullet-shape seam (`_shard` in `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`).
- Code-drawn lime fan icon (`drawShardSwarmIcon`, `src/powerups/icons.ts:1121`).

Missing:
- **No fire SFX.** `playWeaponFireSound()` (`src/audio/effects.ts:628`) has no `shard_swarm` case, so it falls through to the `default:` no-op — the weapon fires silently in live play, in the hold-full metronome and in every gym.
- **No muzzle flash.** The definition declares no `muzzleFlash` metadata, and `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:896`) only spawns the launch cue `if (def.muzzleFlash)`.
- **No per-weapon impact feedback.** No `impactFx` spec, so `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()` returns early: no baked hit cue (the impact is silent) and only the generic warm-white flash (`spawnBulletImpact`, `0xfff2a0`, r7, `CombatScene.ts:434`) rather than a lime shard-coloured one. The fan therefore reads as weak noise against the neon background at 0.72× bullet scale.

## Goal (user story)

As a player holding the Shard Swarm, I want an audible launch and hit so I can hear that the five-shard fan is firing and connecting, and I want the shards and their impacts to punch clearly against the neon field, so the weapon feels as distinctive in the hand as its silhouette suggests — without any change to its balance.

## Scope

`shard_swarm` only. Feel/visual/audio only — no behaviour or balance change: fire rate (750 ms, once per beat), the five offsets (±15°, ±7.5°, 0°), bullet lifetime (0.55 s → ~193 px reach), speed, size and colour stay exactly as they are.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Audible fire.** `playWeaponFireSound('shard_swarm')` routes to a new baked ToneForge fire cue (recipe `aihell-shard-swarm-fire`, rendered by `scripts/build-audio.sh`), so live fire, the hold-full metronome and gym fire all sound identical through the one shared path (`src/audio/effects.ts`, `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES`-adjacent registry pattern).
- **Audible, visibly distinct impact.** `shard_swarm` declares an `impactFx` spec (`color` = lime-family, `radius`, `duration`, `cue`) resolved through `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()`, producing a lime-tinted impact flash and a new baked hit cue (`aihell-shard-swarm-impact`) so the game and every gym connect identically. The generic white fallback flash no longer applies to this weapon.
- **Muzzle flash + more noticeable in-flight VFX.** The definition declares `muzzleFlash` metadata (lime, sized for a five-shard burst) spawned through the shared `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` → `spawnMuzzleFlash` path, and the shards are made more legible in flight (e.g. slightly stronger rim/spine contrast and/or a brighter trail) through the shared `bulletVisuals` seam — no per-scene copies, no new bespoke rendering path.
- **Gym↔game parity.** All changes land in the shared core/seams (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`, `src/vfx/`, `src/audio/`) and are consumed identically by `PlayScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymWeaponLeveling`; `CombatScene.equivalence` and the gym-parity/documentation roster guards pass unchanged.
- **Docs + audio catalogue updated.** `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` records both new cues with their recipes and seeds, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` lists them, and the per-weapon visual roster guards (`src/utils/weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisualRoster.test.ts`) plus README/GDD §4.4/§7.3 per-weapon notes include the Shard Swarm's fire and impact identity instead of listing it as visual-only.
- **No new legibility regressions.** The five-shard fan at full upgrade levels (extra projectiles, larger bullets) must not become a screen-filling blur: the impact/muzzle flashes are rate-limited by the natural 750 ms cadence and the effect sizes stay within the existing per-weapon effect budget.
- **Full test suite passes**, including new/updated tests for the fire cue dispatch, `impactFx` resolution, muzzle-flash spawn, and the audio cue contract test (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`).

## Key files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `shard_swarm` `muzzleFlash` / `impactFx` metadata
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — ensure the new metadata survives level resolution
- `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts` — in-flight `shard` legibility for the player weapon
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playWeaponFireSound` case + impact cue registry + `playShardSwarm*Sound` exports
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-shard-swarm-{fire,impact}.yaml`, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared spawn/impact seams (consume-only; no new hook needed if the metadata path suffices)
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, README, GDD §4.4 / §7.3

## Known sibling gap (not in this item's scope)

The same missing feel package (`muzzleFlash`, `impactFx`, fire cue) applies to the other four net-new unlock-pool weapons from AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW: `rear_guard`, `broadside`, `railgun`, `heavy_slug`. Railgun SFX is already tracked by Railgun needs SFX (AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA); the remaining three have no item yet. The metadata/pipeline work here should be structured so those can reuse it unchanged.

## Risks / notes

- ToneForge assets are baked, not runtime-synthesised (`src/audio/thrusterShim.ts` is the sole runtime exception): new cues need recipe YAML + a `scripts/build-audio.sh` run, and the seeds must be recorded.
- Audio must remain a safe no-op in headless tests (no audio context).

# Unit tests: player Phase Shift unmistakable layers

Test-first contract for the player path of AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU (approach C,
aggressive activation edge / soft sustained state). Write these as failing
tests first; the implementation children make them pass.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the *unmistakable* player treatment pinned by tests
before it is built, so the layers, magnitudes, toggles and teardown cannot
regress and the no-shake guarantee cannot be silently dropped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pure params model.** `resolvePhaseShiftJuiceParams()` maps every new tunable
  and `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggle verbatim (flash, vignette, distortion burst,
  sustained filter, widened split), with no Phaser import in the pure path.
- **Activation edge (aggressive).** A single `update(true, dt)` rising edge
  creates the full activation layer set — dim + split + surge pair + full-screen
  flash + vignette + the camera-filter distortion burst — exactly once, and a
  second `update(true, dt)` in the same phase does not duplicate any layer.
- **Sustained state (soft).** While active, deterministic `dt` ticks drive the
  split oscillation/flicker/colour-pulse and the sustained filter layer without
  allocating new game objects per frame (asserted by object-count stability
  across N ticks).
- **Exact teardown.** On the falling edge every overlay is destroyed, every
  camera filter added by the treatment is removed from the camera filter list,
  the registry is emptied, and a re-activation cycle produces a fresh, single
  layer set (no leak, no duplicate).
- **Renderer fallback.** With the renderer reporting non-WebGL (or a camera with
  no `filters`), the treatment applies the overlay layers only, never throws and
  never touches a filter API; the same suite passes headless.
- **No camera shake.** The retained regression test still asserts the treatment
  never calls `camera.shake` in any phase of the cycle.
- **Test style.** Deterministic (`dt` ticks, no sleeps/randomness), using the
  shared `VfxStubScene` / `bootScene` harness.
- Player activation edge is an aggressive, structural glitch: a short camera-filter distortion burst plus a full-screen phase flash plus a wider chromatic surge. (verified by this item's tests)
- Exact teardown: the falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera filter, restoring the camera filter list with no residual state or duplicate layer. (verified by this item's tests)
- WebGL capability probe with graceful fallback: filter layers apply only when supported, otherwise degrading to overlay-only layers without throwing. (verified by this item's tests)
- Distinctness and parity preserved: visually distinct from player-death juice, never shakes the camera, gym-game parity guards green, headless no-op safe. (verified by this item's tests)

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.test.ts` — extend.
- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.test.ts` — new (probe/apply/clear contract, shared with the enemy path if reused).

## Notes

Tests must not require a real WebGL context: stub the camera filter list with a
minimal fake exposing `internal`/`external` `add*` factories, `list`, `remove`,
`clear`.

# Camera filter driver with WebGL capability probe

Shared infrastructure for approach C of AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU: Phaser 4 camera
filters are **WebGL only**, so every filter-based layer needs one guarded,
teardown-exact entry point.

## Goal

As a developer, I want a single shared module that can apply and clear the
Phase Shift camera-filter layers safely on any renderer, so the game and the
gyms never diverge and a headless/canvas build can never crash or leak.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Capability probe.** `supportsCameraFilters(scene)` returns true only when
  the renderer is WebGL *and* the camera exposes a usable filter list; it never
  throws for a stub, a missing camera, or a renderer without `type`.
- **Activation burst.** `applyPhaseDistortionBurst(...)` adds the pixelate +
  barrel/displacement wobble controllers for the documented duration, driven by
  the exported tunables (no hard-coded numbers).
- **Sustained layer.** `applyPhaseSustainedFilter(...)` adds the gentle
  sustained layer (low-strength glow/bloom or barrel) and returns handles for
  teardown.
- **Exact teardown.** `clearPhaseFilters(...)` removes and destroys only the
  controllers this module added, restoring the camera's pre-existing filter
  list unchanged (verified by a test that pre-adds an unrelated filter and
  asserts it survives).
- **Degradation.** When filters are unsupported every function is a documented
  no-op returning a falsy/"unsupported" result; nothing is allocated.
- **No per-frame allocation.** Steady-state updates mutate existing controller
  properties only.
- **Documented.** Module-level JSDoc explains WebGL-only behaviour, the fallback

# Player Phase Shift unmistakable treatment

Implementation of the player path for AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU: aggressive on the
activation edge, soft while sustained, never shaking the camera.

## Goal

As a player relying on the automatic Phase Shift, I want the activation to read
as an unmistakable system event — a flash, a distortion hit and a strong
chromatic surge — then settle into a clearly-visible sustained shimmer, so I can
trust the state and time my flying.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Activation edge (aggressive).** The rising edge fires, in the same frame:
  a widened/stronger chromatic-surge overlay pair, a full-screen flash in a
  phase-shift palette (not the death-flash palette), a cyan edge/vignette band
  layer, and the camera distortion burst from `cameraFilters.ts`.
- **Sustained state (soft).** While phased: the vivid pulsing chromatic split
  (raised alpha and offset with the slow oscillation), the edge/vignette bands
  and the gentle sustained camera filter, all pulsing rather than static;
  sustained flicker stays at or below the documented seizure-safety cap.
- **Exact teardown.** Falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera
  filter; nothing is left on screen or in the camera filter list.
- **Toggles and tunables.** Each new layer has a `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggle
  and every magnitude is an exported constant; disabling a layer leaves the rest
  working.
- **No shake.** `camera.shake` is never called (regression test retained).
- **Headless safe.** Without a render context the controller still constructs
  and updates as a no-op.
- **Tests.** The sibling test contract item passes.
- Player activation edge is an aggressive, structural glitch: a short camera-filter distortion burst plus a full-screen phase flash plus a wider chromatic surge. (implemented here)
- Player sustained state stays continuously obvious but soft: pulsing vivid split, cyan edge vignette bands, gentle sustained camera filter, no camera shake. (implemented here)

# In-page fallback probe inflates node RSS above the <512 MiB budget

Discovered during **AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES** (verify fix with full suite and a
manual long-run soak), discovered-from **AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE**.

## Observation

A 5-clip full-run soak (`--count 5 --max-duration 1800000 --diagnostics`,
output written to `/tmp/ah-soak/`) completed every clip, but the process node
RSS peaked at **661.0 MiB** (clip 4 start) — above the documented **< 512 MiB**
target. The peak is not recording growth: it is `peakRssBytes` at the *start*
of a clip, carried over from the **previous** clip's end-of-clip probe, and
every clip's end-of-recording RSS was 320–388 MiB.

Cause: clips 3 (34.9 MiB) and 5 (62.75 MiB) are above the 32 MiB in-page probe
threshold, but their files sat outside the served repository root
(`/tmp/ah-soak/…`), so the probe fell back to the **in-page Blob** path
(documented fallback, reported by `probeSourceReason`). That fallback decodes
up to the 32 MiB retained prefix with `decodeAudioData` in one shot, which
inflates node RSS by a few hundred MiB temporarily. A control run of the same
workload with the output inside the repo root (`capture-output/soak/`,
600 s, 48.43 MiB) used the **streamed** probe and peaked at only **408.9 MiB**.

## Why it matters

The < 512 MiB budget is documented for a full-cap run, and `--output /tmp/…`
is a supported, documented invocation. The *path*-based fallback (and its RSS
cost) is not covered by the parent's stated fallback rationale, which only
sanctions the in-page decode for clips *below* a size threshold.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Document, in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` §Long-run memory budget, that
   the streamed probe needs the output inside the served repository root and
   that the in-page fallback costs a temporary whole-prefix audio decode
   (with the measured 661 MiB batch peak vs 408.9 MiB streamed as the
   evidence), or
2. Make the streamed probe work for outputs outside the served root (e.g. a
   temporary route serving the partial file), restoring the < 512 MiB budget
   for every supported output path.
3. Re-run a > 32 MiB clip with `--output /tmp/…` and record the peak RSS
   against the budget.

## Evidence

Full numbers, per-clip diagnostics and logs: comment on
AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES; diagnostics artefacts under `/tmp/ah-soak/`
(`batch-1..5.diagnostics.json`) and
`capture-output/soak/soak-streamed2.diagnostics.json`.
data.title: In-page fallback probe inflates node RSS above the <512 MiB budget for long clips written outside the served repo root

## Why (context)

`bootWithHordeWave()` in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` never injects an RNG or run seed, so `PlayScene._initRunSeed()` draws a fresh `randomSeed()` each run and `computeHordeSpawns` (`src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts`) places the 16 grunts at RNG-jittered points and times (`HORDE_SPAWN_TIME_JITTER_SECONDS = 0.25`). The horde kill test (`killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once`) therefore runs a different layout every run. Candidate mechanisms in the parent brief (in likelihood order): auto-fire/other-bullet interference, overlapping edge grunts, wave-timeout transition (`scene.isTransitioning()`) switching `tick()` to the carried-survivor-only collision pass, or a `paused` no-op tick.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `bootWithHordeWave(seed?)` injects `scene.setRunSeed(seed)` before `scene.restart()` so a given seed reproduces the exact horde layout and spawn schedule; `setRng(createSeededRng(seed))` is used only if `setRunSeed` is shown not to drive the layout.

A repeatable seed sweep (temporary harness or committed parametrised test) over a seed range (e.g. 0-999) finds at least one seed where the un-hardened kill leaves `victim.alive === true` and/or `wm.enemiesAlive !== total - 1`, or proves none reproduces within the range with the sweep evidence recorded.

4. The sweep never modifies production code or shipped assertions; temporary harness code is removed or gated off before the branch is submitted.

- Extend `bootWithHordeWave` with an optional `seed` parameter and inject it via `setRunSeed` before `scene.scene.restart()` (import nothing new — `setRunSeed` is a public seam on PlayScene).
- Add a temporary sweep harness (own `describe`/`it` or local script) iterating seeds 0..999: boot → `releaseHorde` → pick victim → `spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0)` → `tick(0.001)` → check `victim.alive` and accounting; log seed, layout, and phase at failure.
